cards.q: What do mmap and munmap do?
cards.a: Map or unmap files or devices into memory.
A new mapping in the virtual address space of the calling process.

cards.q: Which header must be included to use mmap()?
What does the flags argument of mmap() determine?
cards.a: Whether updates are visible to other processes mapping the same region, and whether updates are carried through to the underlying file.

cards.q: What happens when addr is NULL in mmap()?
cards.a: The kernel chooses the page-aligned address at which to create the mapping.

cards.q: How does the Linux kernel treat a non-NULL addr in mmap()?
cards.a: As a hint, picking a nearby page boundary at or above /proc/sys/vm/mmap_min_addr.
The address of the new mapping.

cards.q: How are the contents of a file mapping initialised?
cards.a: Using length bytes starting at offset in the file referred to by the file descriptor fd.

cards.q: What can be done with the file descriptor immediately after mmap() returns?
cards.a: It can be closed without invalidating the mapping.

cards.q: What constraint applies to the length argument of mmap()?
Which way of creating a new mapping is described as the most portable?
What alignment must the offset argument of mmap() satisfy?
cards.a: It must be a multiple of the page size returned by sysconf(_SC_PAGE_SIZE).

cards.q: What constraint applies to prot relative to the file?
cards.a: It must not conflict with the open mode of the file.
